- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., 0.2–0.4) after a rally, model fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods ahead.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5 days); apply 1–2% downward bias for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8, 0.2, 0.8), model exhibits oscillation bias; use sentiment-weighted average to dampen extremes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast > 82 for 3+ consecutive days, apply 2–4% downward correction.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
